extracted.intended_audience: federal statisticians, statistical practitioners, policy makers, and members of professional statistical societies (e.g., ASA)
extracted.subtask_description: Analyze and map alignment between the ASA Ethical Guidelines for Statistical Practice (2022) and U.S. federal guidance for official statistics (OMB SPD 1, SPD 2/2a, NASEM Principles & Practices, and OMB Data Ethics Tenets). Produce detailed comparisons and identify areas of congruence, tension, and gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Professional Integrity & Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional integrity and accountability require taking responsibility for one’s work. Ethical statistical practice supports valid and prudent decision making with appropriate methodology. The ethical statistical practitioner represents their capabilities and activities honestly, and treats others with respect. (12 elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary ASA EG principle supporting many federal standards; emphasizes honesty about capabilities, responsibility for methodological choices, respectful treatment of others, and support for valid/prudent decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Integrity of data and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethical statistical practitioner seeks to understand and mitigate known or suspected limitations, defects, or biases in the data or methods and communicates potential impacts on the interpretation, conclusions, recommendations, decisions, or other results of statistical practices. (7 elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes obligations to assess and disclose limitations, bias, and impacts on inference; mapped frequently to SPD2 methodological and processing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Responsibilities to Stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who fund, contribute to, use, or are affected by statistical practices are considered stakeholders. The ethical statistical practitioner respects the interests of stakeholders while practicing in compliance with these Guidelines. (8 elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies consideration of stakeholder needs and harms when producing and disseminating statistics; used in alignment tables to assess support for federal dissemination and relevance responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Responsibilities to research subjects, data subjects, or those directly affected by statistical practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethical statistical practitioner does not misuse or condone the misuse of data. They protect and respect the rights and interests of human and animal subjects. These responsibilities extend to those who will be directly affected by statistical practices. (11 elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses confidentiality, privacy, harm-minimization, consent/contextual impacts; aligns closely with SPD1 responsibility to protect trust of information providers and OMB Data Ethics Tenets on privacy and respect for individuals and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. Responsibilities to members of multidisciplinary teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical practice is often conducted in teams made up of professionals with different professional standards. The statistical practitioner must know how to work ethically in this environment. (4 elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on ethical collaboration across professions, clarifying roles/responsibilities and respecting other discipline standards; relevant when federal programs integrate data science, programmatic, and domain expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: F. Responsibilities to Fellow Statistical Practitioners and the Profession
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical practices occur in a wide range of contexts. Irrespective of job title and training, those who practice statistics have a responsibility to treat statistical practitioners, and the profession, with respect. Responsibilities to other practitioners and the profession include honest communication and engagement that can strengthen the work of others and the profession. (5 elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers collegial behavior, honest critique, mentorship, and protection of the profession's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: G. Responsibilities of Leaders, Supervisors, and Mentors in Statistical Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical practitioners leading, supervising, and/or mentoring people in statistical practice have specific obligations to follow and promote these Ethical Guidelines. Their support for – and insistence on – ethical statistical practice are essential for the integrity of the practice and profession of statistics as well as the practitioners themselves. (5 elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies leadership duties to enforce and model ethical practice, implement controls, and support staff development; ASA Appendix organizational duties are grouped with this in alignment tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: H. Responsibilities regarding potential misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethical statistical practitioner understands that questions may arise concerning potential misconduct related to statistical, scientific, or professional practice. At times, a practitioner may accuse someone of misconduct, or be accused by others. At other times, a practitioner may be involved in the investigation of others’ behavior. Allegations of misconduct may arise within different institutions with different standards and potentially different outcomes. The elements that follow relate specifically to allegations of statistical, scientific, and professional misconduct. (8 elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on handling allegations, investigations, and the responsibilities of accused and accusers; links to procedural and institutional contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: APPENDIX: Responsibilities of organizations/institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever organizations and institutions design the collection of, summarize, process, analyze, interpret, or present, data; or develop and/or deploy models or algorithms, they have responsibilities to use statistical practice in ways that are consistent with these Guidelines, as well as promote ethical statistical practice. (Organizations 7 elements; Leaders 5 elements; 12 elements total)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on institutional obligations (governance, policies, controls, promotion of ethical practice) and is treated alongside Principle G in alignment assessments because of overlapping leader/organization duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD1 Responsibility 1: Produce and disseminate relevant and timely information
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce and disseminate relevant and timely information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB SPD1 frames core goals of federal statistical agencies; R1 often aligns with ASA principles about stakeholder relevance and dissemination but can raise tensions with privacy/confidentiality tenets when timeliness conflicts with protection of respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD1 Responsibility 2: Conduct credible and accurate statistical activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct credible and accurate statistical activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes methodological rigor and credibility; maps to ASA B (Integrity of data and methods) and NASEM commitments to quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD1 Responsibility 3: Conduct objective statistical activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct objective statistical activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stresses objectivity and independence in statistical production; links to NASEM Principle 4 (independence) and ASA A (professional integrity).

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD1 Responsibility 4: Protect the trust of information providers by ensuring the confidentiality and exclusive statistical use of their responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect the trust of information providers by ensuring the confidentiality and exclusive statistical use of their responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core confidentiality mandate for federal statistical agencies; strongly aligns with ASA D and OMB Data Ethics Tenet T3 (respect privacy and confidentiality).

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 1.1: Survey planning (Develop a written plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey planning — Develop a written plan (A.1 Methodological plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires articulating objectives and methods up front; aligns with SPD2a methodological plan and ASA guidance on methodological transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 1.2: Survey design (Develop a survey design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey design — Develop a survey design (Sample selection, design choices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sample design and decisions that affect relevance and accuracy; ties to SPD2a sample selection and ASA B on methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 1.3: Survey response rates (Design the survey to achieve the highest practical rates of response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey response rates — Design the survey to achieve the highest practical rates of response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses response rate targets and strategies; linked to equitable treatment of respondents and ASA principles on respecting data providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 1.4: Pretesting survey systems (Agencies must ensure that all components of a survey function as intended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pretesting survey systems — Agencies must ensure that all components of a survey function as intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers cognitive testing and system pretests (SPD2a); supports data quality and transparent methods (SPD2a A.4–A.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 2.1: Developing sampling frames
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing sampling frames — Ensure that the frames for the planned sample survey or census are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame quality affects representativeness and bias; SPD2 requires appropriate framing and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 2.2: Required notification of potential survey respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Required notification to potential survey respondents — Agencies must ensure that each collection instrument clearly states required information (purpose, uses, burden, contacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports informed respondents and transparency; connects to ASA D and survey Q&A obligations about voluntariness and confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 2.3: Data collection methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collection methodology — Balance quality against error; minimize burden/cost and select appropriate collection modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires methodological choices that weigh burden, cost, and data quality; relates to ASA A/B and OMB ethics tenets on minimizing harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 3.1: Data editing (Agencies must edit data appropriately)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data editing — Agencies must edit data appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers procedures to correct/clean data while preserving integrity; links to transparency about edits and ASA B on integrity of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 3.2: Nonresponse analysis and response rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonresponse analysis and response rate calculation — Evaluate and account for nonresponse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires analysis of nonresponse bias and transparent reporting of response metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 3.3: Coding (Coding QUALITY FOR OTHERS TO USE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coding — Ensure coding quality so data are usable by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes producing documentation and codebooks, consistent coding rules, and reusability; maps to ASA expectations for documentation and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 3.4: Data protection (AVOID DISCLOSURE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data protection — Avoid disclosure; protect confidentiality during processing and dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes operational disclosure avoidance methods and controls; central for aligning with ASA D and OMB Data Ethics Tenet T3.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 3.5: Evaluation (Agencies must evaluate the quality of the data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation — Agencies must evaluate the quality of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates ongoing evaluation and quality assessment practices; ties to NASEM Practice 6 (evaluation processes) and ASA B.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 4.1: Developing estimates and projections (USING THEORY AND METHODS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing estimates and projections — Use appropriate theory and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires methodological rigor in estimation and projection; aligns with ASA emphasis on appropriate methodology and NASEM standards for credible inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 5.1: Analysis and report planning (Agencies must develop a plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis and report planning — Agencies must develop an analysis and reporting plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning analysis and intended products improves transparency and reduces analytic flexibility (degrees of freedom).

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 5.2: Inference and comparisons (USE ACCEPTABLE STATISTICAL PRACTICE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inference and comparisons — Use acceptable statistical practice for inference and comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages established inferential methods and transparent reporting of limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 6.1: Review of information products (REVIEW WHAT IS DISSEMINATED & COMPLY WITH OMB GUIDANCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review procedures — Review information products before dissemination and comply with OMB guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates pre-release review processes to ensure accuracy, compliance, and appropriate disclosure avoidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 7.1: Releasing information (USE A PLAN THAT IS EQUITABLE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Releasing information — Use an equitable release plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses timing, equity of access, and release protocols; relates to ASA responsibilities around stakeholders and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 7.2: Data protection and disclosure avoidance for dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Data protection and disclosure avoidance for dissemination — Implement disclosure avoidance strategies for published products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers technical disclosure avoidance, masking, and privacy-preserving dissemination methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 7.3: Survey documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey documentation — Provide documentation for surveys and information collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires metadata, methods, codebooks, and documentation that enable reproducibility and appropriate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 Standard 7.4: Documentation and release of public use microdata
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation and release of public-use microdata — Provide appropriate documentation and apply disclosure avoidance for microdata releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates thorough documentation and protective measures for public-use files.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.1: Methodological plan
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD2a — Methodological plan (part of cognitive interview guidance and pretesting standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the need for a written methodological plan as part of cognitive interviewing and pretesting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.2: Sample selection
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD2a — Sample selection (for cognitive interviews and pretests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires transparent selection and documentation for cognitive interview samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.3: Interview guide
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD2a — Interview guide (use a structured guide for cognitive interviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures reproducible cognitive interview protocols and supports transparent instrument evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.4: Analysis of cognitive interviews (Systematic Analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD2a — Systematic analysis of cognitive interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires documented, systematic methods for analyzing cognitive interview findings (A.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.5: Transparent analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD2a — Transparent analysis of pretest and cognitive interview results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for clear reporting of analyses and decisions based on cognitive interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.6: Final reports
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD2a — Final reports from cognitive interview/pretest activities (A.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires completion and archiving of final methodological reports documenting pretesting process and findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.7: Reporting results
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD2a — Reporting results (A.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates reporting of cognitive interview findings and how they informed instrument changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 1: Relevance to policy issues and society
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle 1. Relevance to policy issues and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure statistical products address societally relevant questions and policy needs; mapped to ASA C and SPD1 R1.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 2: Credibility among data users and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle 2. Credibility among data users and stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote methodological soundness and transparency to maintain credibility; links to ASA A/B and SPD1 R2.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 3: Trust among the public and data providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle 3. Trust among the public and data providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on confidentiality, ethical use, and maintaining provider trust; aligns with ASA D and SPD1 R4.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 4: Independence from political and other undue external influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle 4. Independence from political and other undue external influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages legal and operational safeguards to preserve statistical independence; tied to SPD1 R3 and ASA principles on integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 5: Continual improvement and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle 5. Continual improvement and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevates continual methodological improvement and innovation as a core principle; connects to ASA recommendations for staying current (professional development).

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 1: A clearly defined and well accepted mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 1. A clearly defined and well accepted mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency mission clarity supports relevance and accountability; used in alignment considerations with ASA leadership responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 2: Necessary authority and procedures to protect independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 2. Necessary authority and procedures to protect independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational/legal arrangements to safeguard independence; links to SPD1 and ASA leadership duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 3: Commitment to quality and professional standards of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 3. Commitment to quality and professional standards of practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional commitment to methodological and ethical standards; aligns with ASA A and B and SPD2 quality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 4: Professional advancement of staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 4. Professional advancement of staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training, career development, and staff support to maintain high-quality statistical work; relates to ASA G and organizational appendix items.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 5: An active research program
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 5. An active research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages internal research to support methodological advancement and adaptation to new data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 6: Strong internal and external evaluation processes for an agency’s statistical programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 6. Strong internal and external evaluation processes for an agency’s statistical programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates evaluation, review, and quality assessment processes (aligns with SPD2 3.5 evaluation and SPD2 6.1 review procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 7: Coordination and collaboration with other statistical agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 7. Coordination and collaboration with other statistical agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports comparability, shared standards, and interagency coordination; linked to SPD1 and ASA C on stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 8: Respect for data providers and protection of their data
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 8. Respect for data providers and protection of their data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly emphasizes protection of providers and their data; aligns with SPD1 R4 and ASA D.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 9: Dissemination of statistical products that meet users’ needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 9. Dissemination of statistical products that meet users’ needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on user-centered dissemination, accessibility, and clarity; maps to SPD2 dissemination and ASA C.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 10: Openness About Sources and Limitations of the Data Provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice 10. Openness about sources and limitations of the data provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates transparency about data provenance, limitations, and appropriate uses; aligns with ASA B and SPD2 documentation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T1: Uphold applicable statutes, regulations, professional practices, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: T1. Uphold applicable statutes, regulations, professional practices, and ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad tenet ensuring legal/regulatory/ethical compliance; the paper notes DET1 aligns with many SPD elements and cautions about tensions with dissemination responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T2: Respect the public, individuals, and communities
rubrics_metrics.description: T2. Respect the public, individuals, and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places obligations to consider harms and impacts on groups and communities; used to evaluate potential conflicts with timeliness/relevance mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T3: Respect privacy and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: T3. Respect privacy and confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central duty to protect privacy in collection, processing, and dissemination; strongly aligned with SPD1 R4 and ASA D.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T4: Act with honesty, integrity, and humility
rubrics_metrics.description: T4. Act with honesty, integrity, and humility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical comportment expectations for practitioners; complements ASA A and NASEM credibility principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T5: Hold oneself and others accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: T5. Hold oneself and others accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages accountability mechanisms and reporting; overlaps with ASA H on misconduct and NASEM evaluation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T6: Promote transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: T6. Promote transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates openness about methods, provenance, and limitations; links to SPD2 documentation and NASEM Practice 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T7: Stay informed of developments in the fields of data management and data science
rubrics_metrics.description: T7. Stay informed of developments in the fields of data management and data science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires continuing professional development and monitoring of emerging techniques and risks; aligns with ASA recommendations for staying current.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD3: Principal Federal Economic Indicators related standards (selection and release practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD3 items referenced include: designation of principal indicators, prompt release, release schedule, announcement of changes, release procedure, preliminary estimates and revisions, granting of exceptions, performance evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapped against ASA EG principles in the paper (Table e), showing which ASA principles support SPD3 standards and where considerations (items) should be kept in mind while complying with standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD4: Release and Dissemination of Statistical Products standards
rubrics_metrics.description: SPD4 items referenced include: implement consistent with relevant Statistical Policy Directives; definition of statistical products; definition of statistical purpose; timely release; timely public notification; dissemination; announcement of changes; revisions and corrections of data; exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper maps SPD4 standards to ASA EG principles (Table f) and notes where ASA principles should be considered when meeting SPD4 standards; highlights potential tensions between dissemination/timeliness and privacy/respect tenets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions and Answers When Designing Surveys: required public-facing disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Items for information collections (per OMB Q&A): reasons information is collected; how information will be used and serve agency needs; estimate of average burden and contact; whether responses are voluntary/mandatory; nature and extent of confidentiality provided; duration of respondent involvement; if collecting sensitive information, specify types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mandated disclosures are tied to SPD2 documentation and SPD2a cognitive interview standards; mapped to ASA elements that support dignity, respect for data providers, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degrees of Freedom Analysis / Code assignment / Coding schema (analytic transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis topics in paper include Degrees of Freedom Analysis, code assignment, and coding schema — i.e., the need to document analytic decisions, code, and coding schemas to reduce undisclosed analytic flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper discusses how documenting degrees of freedom and code/coding schemas supports ASA and federal requirements for transparency and reproducibility; relevant to SPD2 3.3 (coding) and SPD2a transparency standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and Coding Schema for Comparing Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper uses an alignment model coding schema to identify goals, activities, and manner within guidelines and to code alignment across documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a methodological rubric applied in the paper to systematically map items from ASA EG to SPD1/2/2a, NASEM, and OMB Data Ethics Tenets; includes simplified coding sheet and detail tables.
